blocks.text: FINAL EXPERIMENT REPORT  |  13 OCTOBER 2026  |  EMM PROJECT

This report consolidates the completed analyses of reciprocity and next-month return in Reddit reply networks. The main search and robustness comparisons are complete for the implemented activity-based specification. The results describe associations and are not estimates of causal effects.

rows: Temporal and reciprocity EDA; pooled model; 2,046 community models
Activity selectors, local discretization; 347 valid groups; top 10 reported
Binary versus proportional; separate searches, top-10 overlap and reference differences
Full raw-data audit found no repeated-reply intensity
Ordinary versus user-clustered inference; reference plus fixed top 10
Binary AMEs; reference plus fixed top 10; ranking and direction checks

blocks.text: What the experiments establish
1. Adjusted reciprocity-return associations are negative in the reference and in 347 of the 347 activity subgroups evaluated in M.

2. A separate search with proportional reciprocity shares 0 of 20 distinct top-ten descriptions with the binary search; the direction of the subgroup-reference difference agrees in 20 of the 20 top-ten subgroups estimated under both measures.
3. User clustering modestly widens uncertainty. Probability-scale analysis changes the ordering of the strongest subgroup differences.

Scope: months 1-10; activity selectors only; no lagged controls or community-context selector search. The weighted variant is unavailable in the supplied data. See pages 8-9 for limits and reproduction.

The analysis contains 36,031,393 user-subreddit-month observations from 3,354,982 users across 2,046 subreddits. The next-month return rate is 36.39%. Eleven monthly networks provide ten observed transitions; month 11 supplies the last return label.
Variables and fitted model

Return means appearing as a reply author in the same subreddit in the following month. Binary reciprocity is 1 when reciprocal_partners > 0. Proportional reciprocity is reciprocal_partners / outgoing_partners; this definition was checked on every analysis row.

The logistic model includes reciprocity, ln(1 + replies_sent), ln(1 + replies_received), and month and subreddit fixed effects. Subgroup models use the same specification within each subgroup. The global reference uses the full analysis population, including the subgroup.

Sent and Received throughout this report refer to the existing replies_sent and replies_received fields. The raw adjacency lists contain no repeated targets, so these supplied network counts do not retain repeated-message intensity.
Completed foundation

Temporal EDA found predominantly short-lived or intermittent participation. Across subreddits, extending the return window from one to three months increased return rates by an unweighted mean of 14.34 percentage points. This EDA does not change the one-month outcome used in M and A1-A3.

Unadjusted return rates were 44.37% with binary reciprocity and 27.66% without it, a 16.71-percentage-point difference. After adjustment, the pooled coefficient was -0.2413, with clustered 95% CI [-0.2435, -0.2390]; the odds ratio was 0.786 and the binary AME was -4.44 percentage points. Raw group differences and adjusted model estimates represent different comparisons.

Separate community models converged for all 2,046 subreddits. Coefficients were negative in 2,021 and positive in 25; nominal 95% intervals lay below zero in 1,782 and above zero in three. The remaining 261 included zero. The median AME was -6.33 percentage points (IQR -8.25 to -4.55). These comparisons were exploratory and unadjusted for multiple testing.
Sources: ../network_eda/; ../eda_outputs/figures/; ../logistic_resgression/pooled_logistic.ipynb; ../logistic_resgression/results/subreddit_logistic_results.csv; A2 and A3 reference checkpoints.

Numeric selectors are discretized locally, following the 3-lbca strategy of Meeng and Knobbe (2021): each time a subgroup is refined, Sent and Received are split into 8 equal-frequency bins of that subgroup, and every cut point gives a <= and a > condition. Beam width is 10, the search has 3 levels, and minimum support is 5,000. A subgroup is skipped when any combination of reciprocity (yes/no) and return (yes/no) has fewer than 10 observations. Reporting k = 10 is distinct from beam width. The quality score is sqrt(n) x |beta_subgroup - beta_reference|.

The binary search returned 347 valid subgroups: 29 with one condition, 192 with two conditions, 126 with three conditions. 347 of the 347 reciprocity coefficients were negative; coefficients ranged from -1.150 to -0.216, against a global reference of -0.2413. The highest-quality subgroup was Sent>1 and Received>1 and Sent<=14 (n = 10,004,049; return rate 55.61%; beta = -0.449; 95% CI [-0.454, -0.444]). Its AME was -9.45 percentage points.

Subgroups overlap; their sizes must not be added. CIs use user-clustered standard errors. Signed delta = subgroup beta minus reference beta. The original CSV field delta is the absolute difference used in quality. More negative signed delta means a stronger negative conditional association.

The weakest negative coefficient among all 347 valid groups was -0.216 for Received>2 and Sent>22 (n = 698,743). 334/347 intervals exclude the reference point. Magnitudes and probability-scale effects are more informative than this diagnostic alone.

Sources: ../beam_search/emm_beam_search_results.csv and M_reference_discovery/tables/top_10_subgroups.csv. AME values are supplied by A3. The subgroup definitions use the same activity variables included as regression controls.

The beam search was repeated with proportional reciprocity as the target, with the same data, model, local discretization and settings. It returned 409 valid subgroups (409 with a negative coefficient), against 347 for binary reciprocity; 147 subgroups were visited by both searches. The two top-ten lists share 0 of 20 distinct descriptions (Jaccard overlap 0.000). Because thresholds are recomputed in every refined subgroup, the two searches follow different paths, so identical descriptions are a strict criterion. By observations, 95% of those selected by the proportional top ten are also selected by the binary top ten (Jaccard overlap of the two selections 0.442). Each subgroup in either top-ten list was also estimated under the other measure: of the 20 that could be estimated under both, the coefficient sign agreed in 20 and the direction of the subgroup-reference difference in 20. Among all 147 subgroups visited by both searches, the direction of the difference agreed in 136.
Proportional reference: beta -0.3728, clustered SE 0.001347, 95% CI [-0.3755, -0.3702].

The table is the union of both top-ten lists, binary top ten first. A rank marked * belongs to a subgroup that the search of that measure did not visit: it was fitted separately, and the rank is the place its quality would take in that search. Betas represent different reciprocity contrasts and are not directly comparable probability changes.
Weighted variant: not applicable to the supplied data

The audit examined all 2,046 JSON files, 22,506 monthly networks and 136,829,959 target entries across 40,050,308 outgoing user-month lists. No list contained repeated targets. A distinct repeated-reply-weighted experiment cannot be recovered from these inputs. This does not imply that users never replied repeatedly in the underlying Reddit activity.
Sources: A1_reciprocity_measure/tables/, reports/ and audits/.

The global reference and fixed binary top ten were refitted once each using the original likelihood and controls. User-clustered CRV1 uncertainty was reproduced, then ordinary model-based (iid) uncertainty was calculated on the same fitted model. All eleven models converged and retained their complete input samples.

User clustering increased the reference standard error by 13.1% and top-ten subgroup standard errors by 2.0%-5.3% (median 3.9%). All ten subgroup confidence intervals remained below zero under both approaches. Coefficients and the quality ranking were unchanged. M already used user-clustered inference; A2 supplies its explicit comparison with ordinary model-based uncertainty.

M ranks refer to the subgroup descriptions on page 3. SE change = 100 x (clustered SE / ordinary SE - 1). Both sets of intervals are pointwise 95% intervals. 10 of the 10 subgroup intervals lie below the reference coefficient under both methods.
Interpretation

Allowing dependence within users modestly widens uncertainty without overturning the negative-association evidence in these selected groups. It is expected that coefficient signs, AME point estimates and quality rankings do not change when only the covariance calculation changes. This comparison does not isolate dependence from every possible source of model misspecification.

A subgroup confidence interval excluding the global reference coefficient is a descriptive diagnostic, not a formal test of the difference between two estimated coefficients. The reference includes the subgroup, so a formal test must account for their joint uncertainty. Intervals are pointwise and have no multiple-testing or post-selection adjustment.

Sources: A2_user_dependence/tables/a2_comparison.csv; reports/summary.json. All ten clustered subgroup fits reproduce M; the reference agrees with the saved pooled notebook. Clustered results remain the basis for interpretation.

sections.title: 5. A3: effects on the probability scale

blocks.text: For binary reciprocity, the AME is the average discrete change in predicted return probability when reciprocity changes from 0 to 1, holding the other model inputs fixed for each observation. An AME of -9.45 percentage points means an average model-predicted change of -9.45 points for that contrast; it is not a 9.45% relative change and is not a causal estimate.

The reference AME was -4.44 percentage points. AMEs for the fixed top ten ranged from -10.14 to -7.25 percentage points. 10 of the 10 subgroup-reference differences had the same direction on the coefficient and probability scales. The Spearman correlation between rankings by absolute coefficient difference and absolute AME difference was -0.697, which shows how far the ordering of effect magnitudes depends on the scale.

M rank is the original size-weighted quality rank. The last two columns rank absolute subgroup-reference differences without size weighting. Reference AME: -4.44 percentage points. Subgroups are identified on page 3.
Which context has the largest probability difference?

The most negative AME is -10.14 percentage points for Sent>1 and Received>1 and Sent<=8 (M rank 9), a difference of -5.71 points from the reference. The highest-quality context, Sent>1 and Received>1 and Sent<=14, has AME -9.45 points and rank 2 of 10 by absolute AME difference.

Each AME is averaged over its own fitted population. Differences therefore reflect both model estimates and covariate composition, rather than a common standardized population. A3 provides point estimates only: no AME confidence intervals or post-selection uncertainty were estimated. Coefficient/AME sign agreement is expected in this binary main-effects specification and is not an independent robustness test.

Sources: A3_probability_scale/tables/top_10_ame_comparison.csv, reports/summary.json and model_checkpoints/. Eleven refits reproduced M's coefficients to numerical precision. Ordinary covariance was used for those point-estimate refits; original clustered coefficient CIs were retained.

Figure 1. The same ten subgroups, indexed by M rank. Left: coefficients and user-clustered 95% intervals; the dashed line is the global coefficient. Right: binary AME point estimates; the dashed line is the global AME. AME uncertainty was not estimated. Separate horizontal scales are intentional.
Figure 2. Percentage increase in SE after user clustering. Ref denotes the global model; 1-10 are M ranks. Both figures use the canonical results tables and can be regenerated without model refits.
Overall interpretation

The positive raw reciprocity-return difference does not persist after adjustment for activity and fixed effects. Negative adjusted associations appear across the activity contexts evaluated. The selected contexts are robust to clustered uncertainty, while the order of effect magnitudes depends on whether coefficients or probability differences are used. Under proportional reciprocity a separate search selects different descriptions, while the direction of the subgroup-reference differences is compared in A1.

Substantive interpretation should report both the coefficient contrast and the AME. A more negative logistic coefficient does not necessarily imply the largest average probability difference. The AME analysis supports directional heterogeneity across the selected activity contexts, but the rank correlation between the two orderings (-0.70) argues against treating the coefficient-based ordering as the sole substantive result.
Limits of the completed experiments

Activity context: subgroup selectors are Sent and Received, which are also regression controls. These results describe variation across activity levels; the search did not include separate community-context variables. Community-specific regressions are supporting analyses, not a community-selector beam search.

Model scope: fitted transitions are 1-10, with contemporaneous activity controls and month/subreddit fixed effects. Lagged controls and the corresponding transitions 2-10 specification have not been run.

A subgroup confidence interval excluding the global reference coefficient is a descriptive diagnostic, not a formal test of the difference between two estimated coefficients. The reference includes the subgroup, so a formal test must account for their joint uncertainty. Intervals are pointwise and have no multiple-testing or post-selection adjustment.

Effect scale and data: AMEs use each group's own covariate distribution and have no uncertainty intervals. Weighted repeated-reply intensity is unavailable. All results remain descriptive; none establishes that reciprocity causes lower return.
What remains for the paper

The experiment report, tables and paste-ready results text are complete. Align the methods with the implemented activity-only, non-lagged specification; if broader selectors or lagged controls remain a requirement, those are additional experiments. Describe weighted A1 as not applicable, retain clustered CIs, explain the two effect rankings, and distinguish interval exclusion of the reference point from a formal difference test.

manuscript_results.txt and manuscript_results.tex contain results prose for M and A1-A3. No manuscript source was edited, and no new experiments were run during packaging. The existing LaTeX tables are included as exported; their layout has not been compiled in the target manuscript.

blocks.text: Rerunning

From the project root, python experiments/code/run_experiment.py A2 prints the command. Add --execute to run it. Choices: M, M-report, A1, A1-weighted-audit, A2 and A3. Added scripts can also run directly at their documented paths. The launcher preserves the original M entry point. Use the recorded analysis environment, including pyfixest 0.60.0.

Generated outputs go directly to tables/, reports/, latex/, audits/ and model_checkpoints/ inside each experiment. A1/A2 share the single parquet cache under A1_reciprocity_measure/data_cache/. The analysis CSV and raw networks remain in their original locations.

To rebuild the report without refitting, run code/build_bundle.py using the analysis Python, then code/render_report.py using a Python with reportlab. The builder reads canonical files and does not copy them. Reruns of experiments may update their generated results; they do not edit original source code.
Original evidence: ../beam_search/emm_beam_search_results.csv, ../network_eda/, ../eda_outputs/figures/ and ../logistic_resgression/. Source references in this report are relative to experiments/.
